title: Manuella & the Boxer: A Play Honoring French Boxing Champion François Pavilla
text:
Discover the captivating story of François pavilla, a French boxing champion whose life is brought to the stage in the new play, “Manuella and the Boxer.” This article delves into the creation of the play, exploring the sources and inspiration behind this “tragic inspiration drama,” and will highlight the triumphs and tribulations of the celebrated boxer’s career. Learn about the legendary boxing career of François Pavilla and the talented team that brought his story to life.
Life of Boxing Champion François Pavilla Takes Center Stage in Martinique A new play, Manuella and the Boxer, explores the triumphs and tribulations of the celebrated French boxer.
Published: April 9,2025
A Theatrical Tribute to a Boxing Legend Fort-de-France ,martinique – The life story of François Pavilla,a triple French boxing champion,is being brought to the stage in a new play conceived by José Alpha. Manuella and the Boxer, a production by TEATLARI – Théâtre des Cultures Créoles, offers a tragic inspiration drama based on the life of the Martinican sportsman.
Gladys Arnaud portrays Manuella,François Pavilla’s wife,in the play. (Benny-Photos) The play premiered Wednesday, April 9, at 7:30 p.m.at Tropiques Atrium in Fort-de-France.
Crafting the Narrative: Sources and Inspiration Playwright José Alpha meticulously pieced together pavilla’s story using a variety of sources:
Slices of life from François Pavilla himself. Interviews with his brothers, Bernardin and nicaise Pavilla. Insights from his daughter, Fabienne Sorin. Archival materials from the Schoelcher library . Memories and testimonies from those associated with the Spirit of Pavilla-Boxing Force of Sainville. this story was built from the slices of life of the Martinican boxer François Pavilla, interviews with his brothers Bernardin and Nicaise Pavilla and his daughter Fabienne Sorin, archives of the Schoelcher library, memories and testimonies of the former of the Spirit of pavilla-Boxing Force of Sainville lands in Fort-de-france.
Production also incorporated family photos and articles from local and national press outlets that covered the boxer’s career.
From trénelle to Champion: Pavilla’s Rise François pavilla’s journey began in the Trénelle district of Fort-de-France.Born Oct. 10,1937,his boxing talent was recognized early on.
it is indeed a young amateur boxer of the Trénelle district of Fort-de-France, born October 10, 1937, spotted by his cousins ​​boxers Théo and Fernand Nolet invited him to enter into mainland France to develop ther, in 1951, at the age of 14, his potential for combat strike in the room of Jean Traxel in Montrouge.
At the age of 14, Pavilla was invited to mainland France to develop his skills, training in Montrouge under jean Traxel.
A Decade of Dominance Pavilla’s career trajectory soared after Jean Bretonnel, a renowned coach, took him under his wing in 1952. By 1964, he had become the champion of France.
Less than a year later, in 1952, Jean Bretonnel, the famous coach manager, took him in his stable where he became 10 years later, in 1964, champion of France, following numerous victories in the category of Welters and Super Welters. His professional record is edifying: 3 times French champion and world vice-champion in the Welters weight category. On March 29,1958,he married manuella Graça at the town hall of the fourth arrondissement of Paris,which will give him 5 children.
His record includes three French championships and a world vice-champion title in the Welterweight division. He married manuella Graça on March 29, 1958, in Paris, and they had five children.
Eric Bonnegrace plays the role of the coach in Manuella and the Boxer. (Benny-Photos) The Creative Team The production team includes (from left to right) José Alpha, Eric Bonnegrace, Gladys Arnaud, laurent Troudart, and José Cloquell. (Benny-Photos) The production team includes playwright and actor José alpha, actors Eric Bonnegrace and Gladys Arnaud, laurent Troudart, and José Cloquell, who is the manager and lighting designer.
See Manuella and the Boxer at Tropiques Atrium in Fort-de-France.
